key_insight: A real-time GW-BSE implementation with atom-centered bases and localized resolution of the identity makes first-principles optical spectra feasible for thousands of atoms.
engineering_relevance: This lowers the computational barrier for designing and screening large optoelectronic materials such as disordered semiconductors, nanostructures, and solar-cell absorbers.
method: Real-time propagation of the GW-BSE equations
Atom-centered basis sets to represent large systems efficiently
Locally optimized real-space resolution of the identity to reduce scaling
evidence_signal: The framework is demonstrated by computing the absorption spectrum of a nanographene system containing 4616 atoms, with per-step cost scaling quadratically in system size.
watch_item: Although much cheaper than conventional GW-BSE, the approach still requires careful implementation and validation for strongly disordered or highly correlated systems.
paper_title: Optical absorption spectra from the $GW$-Bethe-Salpeter framework for thousands of atoms
